1. SPXC exit is now ~24 calendar days / ~18 trading days overdue — the 7th consecutive daily flag (9/8, 9/9, 9/10, 9/16, 9/17, and now 9/18). The 2026-08-25 decision to exit on the defense-rule breach (Kranze Technology Solutions, US military electronics) still has not executed — it's resting on a passive OCA bracket (sell-limit $205 / stop $186.90) that hasn't filled. This doesn't need a price feed to execute: cancel the resting orders and exit at market or an aggressive marketable limit today, regardless of price. A week of daily flags with no action means the email isn't reaching the decision — worth a direct check-in on why this hasn't moved.

2. GOOG stop status still unconfirmed. First flagged 2026-09-10 on unverified snapshots showing GOOG below the $333.90 stop; yesterday's (9/17) report and today's independent search both found web context suggesting it has since traded well clear of that level (near $342-349, per unverified sources) — consistent evidence the 9/10 scare was likely a false alarm. But two days running now, the automated price feed has been fully blocked (see below), so this still cannot be formally closed out. A five-minute IBKR check would resolve it either way.

Two different Buffett Indicator trackers disagree today — GuruFocus/others read ~235%, one live tracker showed 293.6%. Using the ~235% consensus reading, which still puts total market cap at roughly 2.35x GDP — historically a level that has preceded every major drawdown on record. Forward P/E, by contrast, is sitting right at its 10-year median — index-level earnings multiples aren't the stretched part of this market, breadth/mega-cap concentration is.

Implication: keep stops tight and don't add size into strength — the macro backdrop doesn't support leaning aggressive on new entries right now, which lines up with holding cash until the two open-position issues above are resolved.

Last historical episodes at comparable levels: 2000 dot-com peak, 2021 post-COVID bubble peak — see buffett-indicator-history.html.

🟢 SPXC — ⚠️ WATCH. Announced a $410M acquisition of FIS Water (Sep 15); Wolfe Research initiated coverage at Outperform the same day; TipRanks notes analyst opinions are otherwise mixed (Sep 16). This is a bolt-on to the HVAC/water side of the business, not the Kranze defense-electronics segment driving the halal exit — it doesn't change the exit decision, see alert above.

🔄 Rotation Suggestions

None today. The watchlist has no active-conviction name to rotate into, and the priority action on both open positions is completing the SPXC exit and confirming GOOG's stop — not opening anything new.

📚 Today you learned

Bolt-on Acquisitions

A bolt-on acquisition is a smaller purchase folded into an existing business line to add capability or share — different from a "transformative" deal that changes what a company fundamentally is. SPXC's $410M FIS Water buy (announced Sep 15) is a clean example: it bolts onto the existing HVAC/cooling and water-treatment side of the business. It does nothing to the Kranze Technology Solutions defense-electronics segment that's driving your exit decision — a bolt-on this size on a multi-billion-dollar company is a rounding error against total revenue mix. The lesson generalizes: an acquisition only moves your halal segment math when it's large enough to meaningfully shift revenue composition — check it as a % of revenue, not by headline dollar size.

Also today: Coverage initiation — when a new analyst/desk starts publishing a rating on a stock for the first time (like Wolfe Research's Outperform on SPXC), as opposed to updating a rating they already had.

Research output, not financial advice. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Verify halal compliance quarterly on Zoya or Musaffa. Prices: Yahoo Finance JSON API + stooq fallback — all blocked by network egress policy this run, no live price fetched. Generated 2026-09-18 Kuwait time.
